implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: a location marked atomic, a read-modify-write operation (compare-and-swap, fetch-add or exchange), and a memory order attached to every access. The rules that matter: relaxed gives atomicity with no ordering at all (counters only); release on a store publishes everything the thread wrote before it; acquire on a load makes everything the releasing thread wrote before it visible; acq_rel for a read-modify-write that does both; seq_cst when a single total order is needed. One indivisible operation per invariant. Retry with backoff. Verify the platform's operation is lock-free for your type and alignment.
idiom_name: atomic location + CAS/fetch-add with an explicit memory order, plus a backoff retry loop
code_sketch:
state = AtomicWord(0)

def take(v):                       # atomically subtract if enough remains
    while True:
        cur = state.load(relaxed)          # read fast; no ordering needed for the value itself
        if cur < v: return False
        if state.compare_exchange(cur, cur - v, acquire_relaxed=acq_rel, failure=relaxed):
            return True
        backoff()                     # lost the race: re-read, do NOT reuse `cur`
pitfalls: One indivisible operation per invariant - two atomic updates of two fields are not an atomic update of the pair.
compare_exchange_weak may fail spuriously: re-read inside the loop rather than retrying with a stale expectation.
A plain (non-atomic) read inside the protocol removes the happens-before edge it depended on, silently.
Verify the operation is lock-free for this type and alignment, or the progress guarantee does not exist.
